quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads make it hard to stop and easy to skid during turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back at you in these conditions and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: Which statement about BAC (blood alcohol content) is true?

options.text: A breathalyzer test measures a person's BAC.
A chemical test is required to convict someone of driving under the influence.
Physical fitness reduces BAC levels.
Coffee or a cold shower lowers your BAC after drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: A breathalyzer test measures a person's BAC.
questions.explanation: A breathalyzer is a chemical test that measures BAC. A chemical test is not required for conviction. Police testimony about how someone was driving, their appearance, and their behavior is enough.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give cyclists as much space as you can. Cyclists have little protection and can be forced off course if you pass too quickly.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving slower than other traffic can also be dangerous because drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: When can you park in a space reserved for people with disabilities?

options.text: Anytime if you have the proper license plates.
Only if you are disabled.
Only if you have the proper license plates and the disabled person named on the registration is in your vehicle.
If someone in your family is disabled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have the proper license plates and the disabled person named on the registration is in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You can only park in a disability space if the vehicle is carrying the disabled person whose name is on the registration or permit.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the roadside. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or sirens approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What factors affect the space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks at objects away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation during driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking your mirrors, and looking at your instrument panel regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead due to heavy fog, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers.
Drive using your parking lights.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, you must turn on your headlights. Use low beam headlights when you are within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle and when within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. In poor weather, always use your low beams.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway begins.
Divided highway ends.
Bumpy road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:

options.text: Road hazard sign.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (or orange in work areas). They warn you of hazardous conditions or special rules ahead.

questions.question: To avoid glare from headlights of an oncoming car:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Avoid the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle by glancing toward the right side of the road. After a brief look to the side, continue watching ahead to track the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When driving in fog with low visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too heavy to see through, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.
